# Architecture

`ms-go-tz-planner` owns authoring, not runtime. It converts untrusted intent or imported real-world text into one strict candidate and deterministically projects the consumer-neutral `technical-task.v1` aggregate from it. TechnicalTask is the source of truth for downstream task semantics: goal, student instruction, expected result, exact concepts, semantic steps, and verification remain separate. No downstream consumer needs to re-analyze task prose with an LLM.

Before generation the service retrieves a bounded canonical target vocabulary from Learning Planner; the model may select only from that input, and TZ Planner subsequently exact-resolves every selected identity. A v1 request is server-bound to the `practice` surface. A v2 request carries only a PII-free orchestration correlation, trigger, exact `practice|project` surface, and optional desired derived difficulty. TZ overwrites any model-authored surface and rejects a desired-level mismatch before verification. It also validates the candidate and TechnicalTask locally, selects an exact sandbox-owned runtime profile, inspects the executable validation contract, and requires a starter/reference/negative executable verification receipt before marking an artifact READY.

The candidate artifact is `practice-task-blueprint.v1`. It is also the normalized persisted source encoding for `technical-task.v1`, avoiding a second conflicting copy of the same semantics. Private fixture files and executable evaluator details remain in the author's private bundle. TZ sends them to Sandbox/Validation for verification and submits the verified candidate and provenance to Practice's dedicated private staging boundary. Practice persists the full blueprint, private evaluation, verification, provenance, and digests as `staged`; the record has no catalog task, public revision, or active state. TZ persists the Practice-owned stage receipt and cannot call Admin publish. Practice approval/materialization is a future explicit workflow.

The follow-up architecture item `PRACTICE_TZ_STAGED_APPROVAL_WORKFLOW` is OPEN. It covers review UX, mapping into reusable catalog entities, approval authority, materialization rules, public activation, revision publishing, and rejection/rework.

Full TechnicalTask and student-safe DTOs are distinct types and routes. The student type has no fields for internal steps, hints, actions, verification, concepts, or private fixtures. See [TechnicalTask contract](technical-task-contract.md).

Pipeline roles are internal responsibilities—Analyze, Design, Learning Requirements, Evaluation Design, and Quality Gates—not separate agents or services. Prompt/model output never becomes authority merely because it conforms syntactically.

The safe internal job projection may expose the bounded orchestration object,
but never the manifest, Student state, private fixtures, or raw provider data.
Planner/Teacher remain responsible for invoking v2; Practice remains responsible
for creating and starting exact immutable task instances.
